heading: Application for IT Graduate Scheme 2027
paragraphs: I am applying for the IT Graduate Scheme at McLaren because it combines the analytical and technical work I already do with the high-performance technology environment I want to build. The opportunity to contribute to major technology initiatives across Core Technology, Data & AI and Product Development is exactly the environment I need to grow. I am available to start in September 2027 and comfortable with the on-site position at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking.

My background combines practical IT support and security work with formal analytical training. I am an MSc Information Security graduate from Royal Holloway, awarded with Merit, with CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity, preceded by a BCA in computer applications. That means I understand not only how to resolve technical problems but how to approach complex challenges in a structured way, which is central to a role that requires problem solving, analytical thinking and data literacy.

In my current IT support position I am the first point of contact for 15 colleagues across 15 to 20 devices, troubleshooting access and system problems, monitoring server health and maintaining network and website-access controls. I handle four to five access requests a day through on-premises Active Directory and investigate four to five suspicious emails a day, recording findings and alerting colleagues to recurring tactics. I also built a local tool that maps Windows error codes to their common causes and used it to trace intermittent server freezes to missing or corrupted DLLs. My technical skills include Python, PowerShell and SQL. I also use AI tools regularly, including Claude, Codex and Hermes, and I designed and built my own AI assistant with their help, which gives me a practical understanding of how AI can be applied to solve real problems.

Two things I want to be straightforward about. I have not worked in IT professionally in the automotive sector, so that formal experience is something I would expect to develop through McLaren's rotational programme rather than claim as existing. However, I bring more than just technical skills. My father has been in the motorcycle automotive business since I was a child, so I grew up around the sector. That shaped my interests from an early age and gave me a genuine understanding of how the automotive business works, including consumer behaviour, lease structures, insurance, warranty, customer care, parts and servicing. I also follow McLaren's F1 team closely. I particularly admire how they continue to improve based on driver feedback, giving both drivers equal upgrades rather than prioritising one, and their mid-season upgrades last year literally changed the game for the team. That approach to continuous improvement and performance is exactly the mindset I would bring to the programme.

What draws me to McLaren specifically is the focus on reshaping how they design, build and support their products through digital transformation. At Co-op, as Person in Charge, I conduct weekly risk assessments and daily compliance checks, and I took the initiative to start maintaining documentation at The Colourful Aura, which has reduced our incident management time by more than half. I am comfortable working under pressure, having handled peak trading hour shifts at Co-op, and I am always learning, most recently through building my own AI assistant with Hermes. The opportunity to contribute through a structured graduate programme with real responsibility and exposure to large-scale systems is exactly the kind of challenge I am looking for. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills and experience could contribute to your team.
